xs-recipes(7) ​

Recipes

Complete, tested workflows — snapshots, safe mirrors, a Raspberry Pi, scheduled backups — with their real output.

ABOUT THESE RECIPES ​

Each recipe below was run against the current binary in a disposable directory, and the output shown is what it printed. Remote recipes went through an ssh stand-in that runs the other side on the same machine, so host:backup/ is a directory next to the source. Replace src/, dst/ and the host names with your own.

DATED SNAPSHOTS ​

Keep one directory per day. Each new snapshot hard-links every unchanged file to the previous day’s copy, so a full-looking snapshot costs only the space of what changed.

Dated snapshots that share unchanged files
sh
snapshot() {
  previous=$(ls -1 snapshots | tail -n 1)
  xs -a ${previous:+--link-dest=../$previous} src/ "snapshots/$1/"
}
snapshot 2026-10-09
printf 'Action items\n' >> src/notes.txt
snapshot 2026-10-10
ls snapshots
stat -c '%h links  %n' snapshots/*/notes.txt snapshots/*/docs/guide.md
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
2026-10-09
2026-10-10
1 links  snapshots/2026-10-09/notes.txt
1 links  snapshots/2026-10-10/notes.txt
2 links  snapshots/2026-10-09/docs/guide.md
2 links  snapshots/2026-10-10/docs/guide.md

notes.txt changed, so each snapshot has its own copy (1 link). guide.md did not, so both snapshots share one file (2 links). Deleting an old snapshot directory frees only the files no other snapshot shares. Treat snapshots as read-only: an in-place write or metadata change to a shared file changes it in every snapshot (shared files).

A SAFE MIRROR ​

Preview first. The dry run prints the same itemized plan the real run will perform, and ends with a one-line summary.

Preview a mirror
sh
xs -ani --delete src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
.d..t...... ./
.d..t...... docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/draft.md
.d..t...... docs/images/
*deleting   docs/images/diagram.svg
*deleting   old/
*deleting   old/a.txt
*deleting   old/b.txt
would transfer 1 files (6B), delete 4

If the plan is what you expect, run it with a deletion limit somewhat above the planned count. A mistaken source path, such as an unmounted disk, then stops at the limit (exit 25) rather than emptying the destination.

Run the reviewed mirror with a deletion limit
sh
xs -ai --delete --max-delete=10 src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
.d..t...... ./
.d..t...... docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/draft.md
.d..t...... docs/images/
*deleting   docs/images/diagram.svg
*deleting   old/
*deleting   old/a.txt
*deleting   old/b.txt

A RASPBERRY PI, OR ANY HOST WITHOUT XS ​

Build the release binaries once (release binaries), install the helper, then push natively. The installer picks the ARM64 build for a 64-bit Pi.

Install xs on a host that does not have it, then push natively
sh
export XSYNC_RELEASE_DIR=releases
xs --install user@pi
xs -azi --no-fallback src/ user@pi:backup/ | tail -n 3
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
Installed xs-linux-amd64 on user@pi at ~/.local/bin/xs
xs  version 0.1.0  protocol version 4  git d3a49f8872fd
<f+++++++++ notes.txt
cd+++++++++ scripts/
<f+++++++++ scripts/build.sh

Captured through tests/fakessh.sh, an ssh stand-in that runs the remote side on the same machine.

Without the helper, the same push still works but runs rsync, with a notice (troubleshooting). Adding --no-fallback, as here, proves the native path was used.

FILES CHOSEN BY FIND ​

Copy the files find selects, with NUL delimiters
sh
(cd src && find . -name '*.md' -print0) | xs -ai0 --files-from=- src/ dst/
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
cd+++++++++ ./
cd+++++++++ docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/guide.md
>f+++++++++ docs/odd\#012name.md

Run find from inside the source so the names are relative to it, and use -print0 with -0 so any filename survives, newlines included. In the output, xs escapes the newline as \#012. With --files-from, -a does not recurse into listed directories; add -r if the list names directories whose contents you want.

A SCHEDULED BACKUP ​

A scheduled backup that logs and keeps the exit status
sh
cat > backup.sh <<'SH'
#!/bin/sh
log=backup.log
xs -a --delete --log-file="$log" --out-format='%t %i %n' src/ dst/ > /dev/null
status=$?
echo "$(date -u '+%Y/%m/%d %H:%M:%S') finished with exit status $status" >> "$log"
exit $status
SH
sh backup.sh; echo "exit status: $?"
head -n 3 backup.log; tail -n 1 backup.log
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
exit status: 0
2026/10/10 16:32:52 cd+++++++++ ./
2026/10/10 16:32:52 cd+++++++++ archive/
2026/10/10 16:32:52 >f+++++++++ archive/2026-q3.log
2026/10/10 16:32:52 finished with exit status 0

The log gets the same lines stdout would, plus the script’s final status line, and the script exits with xs’s status so the scheduler can alert on failure. Progress stays off on its own, because a scheduler’s stderr is not a terminal. Personal defaults still apply; set XSYNC_CONFIG='' and XSYNC_OPTS='' in the job if they should not.

Run it nightly at 02:30: a crontab line (scheduler configuration, not captured)
sh
30 2 * * * cd /path/to/backups && sh backup.sh
The same with launchd on macOS: ~/Library/LaunchAgents/local.backup.plist (not captured)
xml
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<!DOCTYPE plist PUBLIC "-//Apple//DTD PLIST 1.0//EN" "http://www.apple.com/DTDs/PropertyList-1.0.dtd">
<plist version="1.0"><dict>
  <key>Label</key><string>local.backup</string>
  <key>WorkingDirectory</key><string>/path/to/backups</string>
  <key>ProgramArguments</key><array><string>/bin/sh</string><string>backup.sh</string></array>
  <key>StartCalendarInterval</key><dict><key>Hour</key><integer>2</integer><key>Minute</key><integer>30</integer></dict>
</dict></plist>

A WRAPPER THAT READS JSON EVENTS ​

A Python consumer that ignores diagnostics and reports the outcome
sh
xs -a --delete --progress=json src/ dst/ 2> events.ndjson
python3 - events.ndjson <<'PY'
import json, sys
events = [json.loads(line) for line in open(sys.argv[1]) if line.startswith('{')]
files = [e for e in events if e['type'] == 'file']
done = events[-1]
print(f"{len(files)} files, {sum(e['bytes'] for e in files):,} bytes sent")
print(f"deleted {done['deleted']}, exit {done['exit_code']}, success {done['success']}")
PY
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
5 files, 1,289,005 bytes sent
deleted 1, exit 0, success True

Diagnostics share stderr with the events, so keep only lines that start with {. The last event is always complete once a transfer has started; check the process status too, for failures before it starts. Every field is documented in JSON progress events.

AN OVERNIGHT PUSH ON A SLOW LINK ​

A bandwidth-limited push that gives up on a stalled link
sh
xs -az --bwlimit=2M --timeout=60 --stats src/ host:backup/ | tail -n 4
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
Total bytes received: 138

sent 114,201 bytes  received 138 bytes  1,239,824.17 bytes/sec
total size is 1,289,005  speedup is 11.27

Captured through tests/fakessh.sh, an ssh stand-in that runs the remote side on the same machine.

--bwlimit caps the bytes on the wire after compression, so -z moves more file data within the same budget. --timeout=60 ends the run with exit 30 if the connection stops moving for a minute; keep-alives stop an idle but healthy connection from tripping it. Run it again in the morning: completed files are skipped, and -P would also resume a large file that was cut off.

PRESERVING EVERYTHING ​

Preserve hard links, ACLs and extended attributes (Linux)
sh
xs -aHAXi src/ dst/ | head -n 6
getfacl -c dst/notes.txt | grep nobody; getfattr -d dst/docs/guide.md 2>/dev/null | grep origin || python3 -c "import os; print(os.getxattr('dst/docs/guide.md', 'user.origin'))"
ACTUAL OUTPUT · EXIT 0
cd+++++++++ ./
cd+++++++++ archive/
>f+++++++++ archive/2026-q3.log
cd+++++++++ docs/
>f+++++++++ docs/guide.md
cd+++++++++ docs/images/
user:nobody:r--
b'scanner'

On Linux, -aHAX adds hard links, ACLs and extended attributes to archive mode. On macOS, add -N for creation times and --fileflags for BSD flags: xs -aHAXN --fileflags src/ dst/ (not captured here, because this page is captured on Linux). Remote ACLs need both hosts on the same platform. A macOS ↔ Linux -A transfer falls back to rsync, and rsync rejected the tested cross-platform ACLs too, so fallback is no guarantee of a conversion.
